title: Concurrency patterns
summary: A mutex-protected counter, a bounded worker pool, pipelines, fan-in and cancellation with context.
hints: `SafeCounter`: guard the map with the mutex in **both** methods: `c.mu.Lock(); defer c.mu.Unlock()`. Reads need the lock too. If you skip it, Go either reports `fatal error: concurrent map writes` or the race detector (when this dojo has it) fails the test with a `DATA RACE` report.

`MapParallel`: allocate `out := make([]R, len(in))`. Start `min(workers, len(in))` goroutines (treat `workers <= 0` as 1) that all `range` over a shared `jobs` channel of *indexes*, each writing `out[i] = f(in[i])`: separate indexes mean no two goroutines touch the same element, so no lock is needed. Send every index, `close(jobs)`, then `wg.Wait()`. Results land in order because each goes to its own slot.

Pipeline stages (`Square`, `Evens`) each create their own output channel, start a goroutine that `range`s over the input, and `defer close(out)`: the stage that sends is the stage that closes. `Count(ctx)`: `select { case out <- i: case <-ctx.Done(): return }` in a loop, with `defer close(out)`; a bare `out <- i` would block forever once the consumer walks away (a goroutine leak). `FanIn`: one goroutine per input forwarding into `out`, a `WaitGroup` counting them, and a final goroutine that waits and *then* closes `out` (closing earlier would panic a sender).
